title: 6R80 transmission pump and filter
introduction:
The transmission fluid pump gives the hydraulic system its pressure supply. I follow the fluid’s route first, then use the exploded drawing to see how the pump’s pieces fit that story. Think of the filter as the intake checkpoint and the pan magnet as a separate collector for metallic material.

This overview covers the 6R80 automatic transmission. It explains operation and component identification; it is not a pump removal, rebuilding or pressure-testing procedure.

edits.text: How the pump and fluid filter work

This transmission uses a gear-type pump to supply fluid pressure to its hydraulic system. The torque converter hub turns the inner drive gear, providing the pump’s mechanical drive. The pump assembly contains the following parts:
edits.why: Following the drive from the converter hub explains what turns the pump, separately from the fluid path through it.

edits.text: Pump body containing the inner drive gear and outer driven gear.
edits.why: The drive and driven labels distinguish the gears within the body.

edits.text: The pump draws transmission fluid from the sump formed by the fluid pan, pulling it through the transmission fluid filter. The filter fits into the intermediate plate portion of the pump assembly, where a rubber seal seals the connection. A magnet attached to the pan collects metallic material carried in the fluid.
edits.why: The filter and magnet collect material in different ways. The drawing separates the filter seal from the filter itself and shows the suction connection at the intermediate plate.

I start with the boxed assembled view to locate the filter beneath the pump, then follow the exploded view to distinguish the gears, plates and shaft. Match each callout to the accompanying table; the exploded spacing is for identification, not an assembly instruction.
